text: dsh-anywhere-sync 是一款面向 DSH Web 客户端的配置同步插件，在设置页提供同步控制，并通过 Agent 工具支持查询状态、双向同步、单向拉取或推送。它可在多台机器间同步插件清单、本地插件源码、插件配置与数据、依赖锁文件、其他 profile 文件和技能；各类内容可分别开关。同步时比较本地、远端和上次同步基线，按设定处理冲突，并可定时或启动后自动同步。适合希望让多台机器共享 Harness profile 的用户。需要 Git 和一个 Git 仓库；私有 GitHub 仓库需要访问令牌。

dsh-anywhere-sync syncs selected Harness profile files across machines via settings or an agent tool. Choose plugin manifests, local source, settings, lockfiles, profile files, or skills. It compares changes and handles conflicts. Requires Git; private GitHub repos need a token.
我想把几台电脑上的 Harness 插件配置和 profile 文件同步起来。
能不能在设置页面查看同步状态，并手动拉取或推送配置？
Keep my Harness profile and selected plugin files in sync across my computers.
dsh-anywhere-sync 的功能「多设备配置同步」：比较本地、远端和上次同步状态，按选择的同步项拉取或推送 profile 文件，并依冲突策略处理同一文件的并行修改。可从设置页或 Agent 工具触发。
dsh-anywhere-sync 会把所选配置文件传到用户配置的 Git 远端；GitHub 仓库信息也会通过 api.github.com 查询。私有 GitHub 仓库需提供有相应仓库访问权限的令牌。

dsh-anywhere-sync README · Anywhere Sync for DeepSeek Harness：[](https://github.com/j1kwen/dsh-anywhere-sync/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[](LICENSE)

Sync a Harness profile — installed plugins, plugin configuration, dependency
locks, local plugin source, skills and other profile files — across machines
through **one private Git repository**. Every category is an independent
switch. A change made on one machine lands on the others at their next sync.

[中文说明](README.zh.md)

dsh-anywhere-sync README · Features：- **Six independently selectable sync items** — plugin manifest, local plugin
  source, plugin configuration (`cordis.patch.yml`), dependency lock, other
  profile files, and skills.
- **Three-way comparison** — local, remote and the last synced hash; only a file
  changed on both sides becomes a conflict.
- **Conflict handling** — remote wins (default), local wins, or keep conflicts
  and choose a side per file from the settings page.
- **Backups before every overwrite** — the last 10 runs under
  `$DSH_HOME/anywhere-sync/backups/`.
- **Automatic sync** — interval, sync on startup, and install dependencies after
  a pulled plugin manifest.
- **The plugin itself syncs** — source of every `link:`/`file:` plugin is stored
  under `local-plugins/<package>/` and written back to the matching install
  directory on the other machines.
- **No machine paths in the repository** — `link:`/`file:`/absolute specs and
  their lockfile blocks are projected out before anything is pushed.
- **Agent tool** — `anywhere_sync` exposes the same `status` / `sync` / `pull` /
  `push` / `install` operations to the model.
- **UI in Settings → Config Sync** — status, per-

dsh-anywhere-sync README · Install：Requirements: DeepSeek Harness with the Web UI, Node.js 20+, and `git`.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add j1kwen/dsh-anywhere-sync
```

Then restart Harness and open **Settings → Config Sync**.

From a local checkout or the release tarball:

dsh-anywhere-sync README · Quick start：1. Create a **private** Git repository for the synchronized configuration.
2. Create a Personal Access Token with `repo` (classic) or Contents read/write
   (fine-grained) access to it.
3. Open **Settings → Config Sync**, enter the repository URL, branch and token,
   then choose **Save and connect**.
4. Choose **Sync now**. On another machine, install this plugin, enter the same
   repository and token, and sync.
5. Enable **Scheduled sync** or **Sync on startup** to keep the machines
   converged.

dsh-anywhere-sync README · Quick start：After a pull that changes the plugin manifest, dependency install and a Harness
restart are required before the new plugins load.

dsh-anywhere-sync README · What syncs：| Item | Local source | Repository path | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Plugin manifest | `<profile>/package.json` | `profile/<profile>/package.json` | on |
| Local plugin source | directories of `link:` / `file:` / absolute dependencies | `local-plugins/<package>/…` | on |
| Plugin configuration | `<profile>/cordis.patch.yml` | `profile/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml` | on |
| Plugin data | files under `$DSH_HOME` listed in the settings page | `plugin-data/<path>` | on |
| Dependency lock | `<profile>/pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | same | on |
| Other profile files | remaining profile config (presets, `config.toml`, …) | `profile/<profile>/…` | off |
| Skills | `~/.agents/skills/`, `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` | `skills/…` | off |

dsh-anywhere-sync README · What syncs：Files that look like credentials (`.env*`, `*credential*`, `*secret*`,
`id_rsa*`, `*.pem`, `.npmrc`, `config.toml`, …) are excluded even when "Other
profile files" is on. A disabled item is neither read, written nor deleted.

dsh-anywhere-sync README · Local plugin source：`package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` are projected into a portable form before
comparison or push: `link:`, `file:`, `workspace:` and absolute-path specs
(including the `link:` install of this plugin itself) are removed, together
with their bundle entries. When a remote manifest is pulled, local links are
merged back in, so each machine keeps its own install paths.

The source of every other local dependency is carried under
`local-plugins/<package>/`. On pull:

dsh-anywhere-sync README · Local plugin source：**This plugin itself is excluded by default.** Its own source is not carried in
the shared repository, so a local development copy cannot overwrite a
GitHub-installed copy on another machine. The switch under **Settings → Config
Sync → Exclude this plugin itself** controls it; the plugin's own settings live
in `$DSH_HOME/anywhere-sync` and are never synced.

New machines still install this plugin once to get the settings page and the
initial sync.

dsh-anywhere-sync README · Plugin data：Some plugins keep their settings outside `cordis.patch.yml`, in files under
`$DSH_HOME`. The **Plugin data** item syncs the files or directories listed in
the settings page to `plugin-data/<path>`.

dsh-anywhere-sync README · Plugin data：Defaults are dsh-whale-widget's `.dshw-size.json` (appearance/switches),
`.dshw-bubble.json` (bubble layout) and `.dshw-api.json` (custom model
registry). Its accounting ledger `.dshw-usage.json`, per-turn sequence and
stats caches are **not** included: they are data, not configuration, and
whole-file sync would mix machines' ledgers. Add other plugin config paths in
the UI; a trailing `/` syncs a directory, and paths must stay relative to
`$DSH_HOME`. Credentials, sessions, storages and this plugin's own state are
rejected.

dsh-anywhere-sync README · How it works：```text
fetch origin <branch> → reset --hard (the mirror is the remote truth)
  ↓ compare hash(local) / hash(remote) / hash(base) per file
  ├─ only local changed  → write into the mirror, commit, push
  ├─ only remote changed → write into the profile (backup first)

dsh-anywhere-sync README · How it works：Every push stages exactly the paths the run changed, so unrelated files in the
same repository (another profile, another tool) are never touched. A push that
loses a race with another machine is recomputed and retried once — never forced.

State lives in `$DSH_HOME/anywhere-sync/` (`config.json`, `state.json`,
`credentials.json`, `repo/`, `backups/`). The synced profile is the profile the
plugin is mounted in; the settings page shows its name.

dsh-anywhere-sync README · Security：- The token is stored on this machine only, in
  `$DSH_HOME/anywhere-sync/credentials.json` with mode `0600`. It is passed to
  git through a scoped `GIT_ASKPASS` environment variable, never written to the
  repository, a URL, a log or a browser response.
- Alternative token sources: `ANYWHERE_SYNC_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- The HTTP API under `/anywhere-sync/api` reuses Harness Connection's Host/Origin
  and browser-login checks, falls back to loopback-only when that service is
  absent, and requires a same-origin `Origin` on mutating requests.
- Synced files, account credentials, sessions and workspaces are separate:
  `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`, session logs and workspace data are never read.
- The agent tool cannot read the token, change the repository, or change the
  selected sync items.
- No telemetry, analytics or outbound requests except the configured Git remote.

dsh-anywhere-sync README · Troubleshooting：1. Restart Harness. Installed client bundles are cached at boot; installing a
   plugin from a Git URL while Harness is running can leave the browser half
   unloaded.
2. Update to 1.2.3 or later. A client-side rendering error is now displayed on
   the page (with a stack) instead of a blank section; the browser console also
   logs the loaded client version.
3. If the page still shows an error, include that message, the browser console
   output, and the Harness version in the report.

dsh-anywhere-sync README · Requirements and supported platforms：- DeepSeek Harness with the Web UI and the plugin manager (the `settings.section`
  and `webServer` services are used).
- Node.js 20+ in the Harness runtime; `git` on `PATH`.
- Designed for macOS, Linux and Windows. CI runs the offline engine and HTTP
  tests on Linux with Node 20 and 22; Windows path handling uses Node's `path`
  APIs but is not exercised by CI.

dsh-anywhere-sync README · Development：```bash
npm run verify   # package/manifest checks + offline engine and HTTP tests
```

The tests create their own temporary bare repositories; they never touch your
profile or the network:

- `scripts/engine-test.mjs` — push, pull, conflict, delete, multi-machine,
  local-link projection, local plugin registration.
- `scripts/http-test.mjs` — admission, same-origin, parameter validation, sync
  lifecycle.

GitHub Actions runs the same checks on every push and pull request.

dsh-anywhere-sync README · Release integrity：- Releases are built from a **signed tag** by GitHub Actions and published as
  `dsh-anywhere-sync.tgz` with `SHA256SUMS`.
- The tarball gets a **Sigstore build provenance attestation**, and the checksum
  file carries a keyless Sigstore signature (`SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json`):

dsh-anywhere-sync README · Release integrity：```bash
  sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
  gh attestation verify dsh-anywhere-sync.tgz --repo j1kwen/dsh-anywhere-sync
  cosign verify-blob --bundle SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json \
    --certificate-identity-regexp 'https://github.com/j1kwen/dsh-anywhere-sync/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/.*' \

- Commits and tags are signed with the maintainer's registered SSH signing key;
  GitHub shows the Verified badge on the commit and tag.

dsh-anywhere-sync README · Limitations：- Text files only; a single file is capped at 5 MiB and larger files are
  reported and skipped.
- Plugin packages themselves are not installed from the repository; the plugin
  manifest and lock are synced, then the profile package manager installs them.
- A pulled local plugin is registered as a dependency but its bundle is not
  enabled automatically (that would reference a package before it is installed).
- `profileFiles` and `skills` are off by default; sync them only after deciding
  what may leave the machine.
- Git submodules, LFS and repository history cleanup are out of scope.
